@gfxCommon.graphics.preset.font.context: Graphics finder (memory shown as bitmaps), Presets dropdown in the toolbar: show memory as the ZX Spectrum 48K ROM's character set, 8×8 pixel characters, 96 of them.

@gfxCommon.graphics.preset.udg.context: Graphics finder, Presets dropdown in the toolbar: show memory as the 21 user-defined graphics (UDG, a ZX Spectrum term; keep the abbreviation) of 8×8 pixels.

@gfxCommon.graphics.preset.screen.context: Graphics finder, Presets dropdown in the toolbar: show memory as the ZX Spectrum's screen (display file) at address $4000.

@gfxCommon.graphics.candidate.font.context: Graphics finder, side list of places where graphics probably are (a heuristic guess): a character set of 96 characters found in memory. Clicking it shows those bytes.

placeholders.address: The start address in hex, e.g. $3D00

@gfxCommon.graphics.candidate.udg.context: Graphics finder, side list of places where graphics probably are: the ZX Spectrum's user-defined graphics area (UDG, keep the abbreviation), which holds 21 graphics.

placeholders.address: The start address in hex, e.g. $FF58

gfxCommon.graphics.candidate.data: Read-only data at {address}, {bytes, plural, one {# byte} other {# bytes}}, read {reads, number}×

@gfxCommon.graphics.candidate.data.context: Graphics finder, side list of places where graphics probably are: a run of data bytes the program read but never wrote or executed. '×' after the count means 'times'.

placeholders.address: The start address in hex, e.g. $C200
placeholders.bytes: The length of the run in bytes
placeholders.reads: How many times the CPU read those bytes in total

@gfxCommon.sprite.type.anchor.context: Sprite Inspector (ZX Spectrum Next), Sprites table, Type column: an anchor sprite (a sprite positioned on its own, which relative sprites attach to). Lower case.

@gfxCommon.sprite.type.anchor4.context: Sprite Inspector (ZX Spectrum Next), Sprites table, Type column: an anchor sprite defined by 4 attribute bytes instead of 5. '4B' abbreviates '4 bytes'; '·' separates the two parts.

@gfxCommon.sprite.type.relComposite.context: Sprite Inspector (ZX Spectrum Next), Sprites table, Type column: a relative sprite of a composite sprite (positioned relative to its anchor, not scaled or rotated with it). 'rel' abbreviates 'relative'.

@gfxCommon.sprite.type.relUnified.context: Sprite Inspector (ZX Spectrum Next), Sprites table, Type column: a relative sprite of a unified sprite (scaled, mirrored and rotated together with its anchor). 'rel' abbreviates 'relative'.

@gfxCommon.sprite.diag.visibleBitClear.c.context: Sprite Inspector (ZX Spectrum Next): short reason chip in the Sprites table saying why a sprite is not shown. Lower case, like the other chips.

gfxCommon.sprite.diag.visibleBitClear.se: Hidden: its visible bit (attr3 bit 7) is clear.

@gfxCommon.sprite.diag.visibleBitClear.s.context: Sprite Inspector (ZX Spectrum Next): the inspector's sentence for why the selected sprite is not shown. 'attr3' is the hardware name of attribute byte 3; keep it.

@gfxCommon.sprite.diag.noAnchor.chip.context: Sprite Inspector (ZX Spectrum Next): short reason chip in the Sprites table. A relative sprite has no anchor sprite before it to attach to.

gfxCommon.sprite.diag.noAnchor.sentence: Hidden: this relative sprite has no anchor before it, so it composes onto an invisible, all-zero anchor.

@gfxCommon.sprite.diag.noAnchor.sentence.context: Sprite Inspector (ZX Spectrum Next): the inspector's sentence for why the selected sprite is not shown.

@gfxCommon.sprite.diag.anchorHidden.chip.context: Sprite Inspector (ZX Spectrum Next): short reason chip in the Sprites table. The relative sprite's anchor sprite is itself not visible.

gfxCommon.sprite.diag.anchorHidden.sente: Hidden: its anchor, sprite #{anchor}, is not visible.

@gfxCommon.sprite.diag.anchorHidden.sent.context: Sprite Inspector (ZX Spectrum Next): the inspector's sentence for why the selected sprite is not shown.

@gfxCommon.sprite.diag.spritesDisabled.c.context: Sprite Inspector (ZX Spectrum Next): short reason chip in the Sprites table. The whole sprite layer is switched off by NextReg $15 bit 0 (keep '$15 bit 0').

gfxCommon.sprite.diag.spritesDisabled.se: Hidden: the sprite layer is off (NextReg $15 bit 0 is clear).

@gfxCommon.sprite.diag.spritesDisabled.s.context: Sprite Inspector (ZX Spectrum Next): the inspector's sentence for why the selected sprite is not shown. 'NextReg $15' is a hardware register name; keep it.

@gfxCommon.sprite.diag.offScreen.chip.context: Sprite Inspector (ZX Spectrum Next): short reason chip in the Sprites table. The sprite is positioned outside the visible area.

gfxCommon.sprite.diag.offScreen.sentence: Hidden: it is at ({x}, {y}), outside the 320×256 sprite space.

@gfxCommon.sprite.diag.offScreen.sentenc.context: Sprite Inspector (ZX Spectrum Next): the inspector's sentence for why the selected sprite is not shown.

placeholders.x: The sprite's X coordinate in sprite space, e.g. 320
placeholders.y: The sprite's Y coordinate in sprite space, e.g. 40

@gfxCommon.sprite.diag.outsideClip.chip.context: Sprite Inspector (ZX Spectrum Next): short reason chip in the Sprites table. The sprite lies outside the sprite clip window (the rectangle the hardware draws sprites in).

gfxCommon.sprite.diag.outsideClip.senten: Hidden: it lies entirely outside the sprite clip window.

@gfxCommon.sprite.diag.outsideClip.sente.context: Sprite Inspector (ZX Spectrum Next): the inspector's sentence for why the selected sprite is not shown.

@gfxCommon.sprite.diag.partlyClipped.chi.context: Sprite Inspector (ZX Spectrum Next): short warning chip in the Sprites table. Part of the sprite is cut off by the clip window or the screen edge.

gfxCommon.sprite.diag.partlyClipped.sent: Partly clipped: {fraction, number, ::percent} of it is outside the clip window or the screen.

@gfxCommon.sprite.diag.partlyClipped.sen.context: Sprite Inspector (ZX Spectrum Next): the inspector's warning sentence for the selected sprite.

placeholders.fraction: The clipped part of the sprite, shown as a percentage, e.g. 25%

@gfxCommon.sprite.diag.patternTransparen.context: Sprite Inspector (ZX Spectrum Next): short warning chip in the Sprites table. Every pixel of the sprite's pattern (its image) is the transparent colour.

gfxCommon.sprite.diag.patternTransparent: Its pattern is entirely the transparency colour ($4B), so nothing is drawn.

@gfxCommon.sprite.diag.patternTransparen.context: Sprite Inspector (ZX Spectrum Next): the inspector's warning sentence. '$4B' is the NextReg that holds the sprite transparency colour; keep it.

@gfxCommon.sprite.diag.patternBlank.chip.context: Sprite Inspector (ZX Spectrum Next): short warning chip in the Sprites table. The sprite's pattern (its image) is one solid colour.

gfxCommon.sprite.diag.patternBlank.sente: Its pattern is a single solid colour.

@gfxCommon.sprite.diag.patternBlank.sent.context: Sprite Inspector (ZX Spectrum Next): the inspector's warning sentence for the selected sprite.

@gfxCommon.sprite.diag.staleAttr4.chip.context: Sprite Inspector (ZX Spectrum Next): short info chip in the Sprites table. A sprite defined by 4 attribute bytes: its stored fifth byte, attr4 (hardware name, keep it), is not used.

gfxCommon.sprite.diag.staleAttr4.sentenc: A 4-byte sprite: its stored attr4 ({value}) is left over from an earlier upload and ignored. It would change this sprite if attr3 bit 6 were set.

@gfxCommon.sprite.diag.staleAttr4.senten.context: Sprite Inspector (ZX Spectrum Next): the inspector's info sentence. 'attr3'/'attr4' are hardware names of attribute bytes 3 and 4; keep them.

placeholders.value: The stored byte in hex, e.g. $0A

@gfxCommon.tilemap.diag.disabled.chip.context: Tilemap Inspector (ZX Spectrum Next): short info chip in the strip of register values. The tilemap layer is disabled.

gfxCommon.tilemap.diag.disabled.sentence: The tilemap is disabled ($6B bit 7 is clear); the inspector shows what it would draw.

@gfxCommon.tilemap.diag.disabled.sentenc.context: Tilemap Inspector (ZX Spectrum Next): tooltip of the chip and the inspector's sentence. '$6B' is a NextReg; keep it.

@gfxCommon.tilemap.diag.overlapMapTiles..context: Tilemap Inspector (ZX Spectrum Next): short warning chip. The tilemap's map bytes share memory with the definitions of the tiles the map uses.

gfxCommon.tilemap.diag.overlapMapTiles.s: The map overlaps the used tile definitions at {ranges}.

@gfxCommon.tilemap.diag.overlapMapTiles..context: Tilemap Inspector (ZX Spectrum Next): tooltip of the overlap chip and the inspector's sentence.

@gfxCommon.tilemap.diag.overlapMapUlaBit.context: Tilemap Inspector (ZX Spectrum Next): short warning chip. The tilemap's map bytes share memory with the ULA screen's pixel bitmap. 'ULA' is a chip name; keep it.

gfxCommon.tilemap.diag.overlapMapUlaBitm: The map overlaps the ULA bitmap at {ranges}.

@gfxCommon.tilemap.diag.overlapMapUlaBit.context: Tilemap Inspector (ZX Spectrum Next): tooltip of the overlap chip and the inspector's sentence. 'ULA' is a chip name; keep it.

@gfxCommon.tilemap.diag.overlapMapUlaAtt.context: Tilemap Inspector (ZX Spectrum Next): short warning chip. The tilemap's map bytes share memory with the ULA screen's colour attributes. 'ULA' is a chip name; keep it.

gfxCommon.tilemap.diag.overlapMapUlaAttr: The map overlaps the ULA attributes at {ranges}.

@gfxCommon.tilemap.diag.overlapMapUlaAtt.context: Tilemap Inspector (ZX Spectrum Next): tooltip of the overlap chip and the inspector's sentence. 'ULA' is a chip name; keep it.

@gfxCommon.tilemap.diag.overlapTilesUlaB.context: Tilemap Inspector (ZX Spectrum Next): short warning chip. The definitions of the tiles the map uses share memory with the ULA screen's pixel bitmap. 'ULA' is a chip name; keep it.

gfxCommon.tilemap.diag.overlapTilesUlaBi: The used tile definitions overlap the ULA bitmap at {ranges}.

@gfxCommon.tilemap.diag.overlapTilesUlaB.context: Tilemap Inspector (ZX Spectrum Next): tooltip of the overlap chip and the inspector's sentence. 'ULA' is a chip name; keep it.

@gfxCommon.tilemap.diag.overlapTilesUlaA.context: Tilemap Inspector (ZX Spectrum Next): short warning chip. The definitions of the tiles the map uses share memory with the ULA screen's colour attributes. 'ULA' is a chip name; keep it.

gfxCommon.tilemap.diag.overlapTilesUlaAt: The used tile definitions overlap the ULA attributes at {ranges}.

@gfxCommon.tilemap.diag.overlapTilesUlaA.context: Tilemap Inspector (ZX Spectrum Next): tooltip of the overlap chip and the inspector's sentence. 'ULA' is a chip name; keep it.

@gfxCommon.tilemap.diag.wrapMap.chip.context: Tilemap Inspector (ZX Spectrum Next): short warning chip. The map runs past the end of its memory bank and continues at the bank's start.

gfxCommon.tilemap.diag.wrapMap.sentence: The map runs past the end of bank {bank} and wraps to its start.

@gfxCommon.tilemap.diag.wrapMap.sentence.context: Tilemap Inspector (ZX Spectrum Next): tooltip of the wrap chip and the inspector's sentence (bank 5, a 16K bank).

gfxCommon.tilemap.diag.wrapMap8k.sentenc: The map runs past the end of bank {bank}'s 8K and wraps to its start.

@gfxCommon.tilemap.diag.wrapMap8k.senten.context: Tilemap Inspector (ZX Spectrum Next): tooltip of the wrap chip and the inspector's sentence, for bank 7, of which the tilemap uses only the first 8K.

@gfxCommon.tilemap.diag.wrapTiles.chip.context: Tilemap Inspector (ZX Spectrum Next): short warning chip. Tile definitions the map uses run past the end of their memory bank and continue at its start.

gfxCommon.tilemap.diag.wrapTiles.sentenc: Tiles the map uses run past the end of bank {bank} and wrap to its start.

@gfxCommon.tilemap.diag.wrapTiles.senten.context: Tilemap Inspector (ZX Spectrum Next): tooltip of the wrap chip and the inspector's sentence (bank 5, a 16K bank).

gfxCommon.tilemap.diag.wrapTiles8k.sente: Tiles the map uses run past the end of bank {bank}'s 8K and wrap to its start.

@gfxCommon.tilemap.diag.wrapTiles8k.sent.context: Tilemap Inspector (ZX Spectrum Next): tooltip of the wrap chip and the inspector's sentence, for bank 7, of which the tilemap uses only the first 8K.

@gfxCommon.tilemap.diag.wrapDefinitions..context: Tilemap Inspector (ZX Spectrum Next): short info chip. A full table of tile definitions would run past the end of its memory bank.

gfxCommon.tilemap.diag.wrapDefinitions.s: A full table of {tiles} tiles from this base would run past the end of bank {bank}; the tiles in use do not.

@gfxCommon.tilemap.diag.wrapDefinitions..context: Tilemap Inspector (ZX Spectrum Next): tooltip of the chip and the inspector's info sentence.

placeholders.tiles: The table's size in tiles, 256 or 512

@gfxCommon.tilemap.diag.below512.chip.context: Tilemap Inspector (ZX Spectrum Next): short info chip. In 512-tile mode every tile is drawn below the ULA screen. 'ULA' is a chip name; keep it.

gfxCommon.tilemap.diag.below512.sentence: In 512-tile mode attribute bit 0 is tile bit 8, so every cell is below the ULA unless $6B bit 0 forces the tilemap on top.

@gfxCommon.tilemap.diag.below512.sentenc.context: Tilemap Inspector (ZX Spectrum Next): tooltip of the chip and the inspector's info sentence. '$6B' is a NextReg; keep it.

@gfxCommon.layer2.diag.off.chip.context: Layer 2 Inspector (ZX Spectrum Next): short info chip in the strip of register values. 'Layer 2' is a hardware layer name; keep it.

gfxCommon.layer2.diag.off.sentence: Layer 2 is not displayed: $123B bit 1 and $69 bit 7 are both clear.

@gfxCommon.layer2.diag.off.sentence.context: Layer 2 Inspector (ZX Spectrum Next): tooltip of the chip. '$123B' is a port and '$69' a NextReg; keep them.

@gfxCommon.layer2.diag.outsideRam.chip.context: Layer 2 Inspector (ZX Spectrum Next): short warning chip. The displayed layer uses memory banks beyond the end of the machine's 2 MB RAM.

gfxCommon.layer2.diag.outsideRam.sentenc: {count, plural, one {Bank {banks} is} other {Banks {banks} are}} past the 2 MB SRAM: the display has no pixels there.

@gfxCommon.layer2.diag.outsideRam.senten.context: Layer 2 Inspector (ZX Spectrum Next): tooltip of the chip.

gfxCommon.layer2.diag.writesShown.chip: writes go to the displayed bank

@gfxCommon.layer2.diag.writesShown.chip.context: Layer 2 Inspector (ZX Spectrum Next): short info chip. The program draws straight into the layer that is on screen.

gfxCommon.layer2.diag.writesShown.senten: The $123B write window maps banks of the displayed layer ($12): drawing shows at once (no double buffering, a tearing risk).

@gfxCommon.layer2.diag.writesShown.sente.context: Layer 2 Inspector (ZX Spectrum Next): tooltip of the chip. '$123B' is a port and '$12' a NextReg; keep them.

gfxCommon.layer2.diag.writesShadow.chip: write window maps the shadow bank

@gfxCommon.layer2.diag.writesShadow.chip.context: Layer 2 Inspector (ZX Spectrum Next): short info chip. The program draws into the shadow (back buffer) layer, not the one on screen.

gfxCommon.layer2.diag.writesShadow.sente: $123B bit 3 maps the shadow layer ($13) into the write window: writes there are not displayed until $12 points at it.

@gfxCommon.layer2.diag.writesShadow.sent.context: Layer 2 Inspector (ZX Spectrum Next): tooltip of the chip. '$123B' is a port, '$12'/'$13' are NextRegs; keep them.

@gfxCommon.layer2.diag.writesPastRam.chi.context: Layer 2 Inspector (ZX Spectrum Next): short warning chip. The memory window the program writes through points beyond the machine's 2 MB RAM.

gfxCommon.layer2.diag.writesPastRam.sent: The $123B write window maps a bank past the 2 MB SRAM: writes through it are lost.

@gfxCommon.layer2.diag.writesPastRam.sen.context: Layer 2 Inspector (ZX Spectrum Next): tooltip of the chip. '$123B' is a port; keep it.

gfxCommon.layer2.diag.sameBanks.sentence: The displayed and the shadow layer are the same banks.

@gfxCommon.layer2.diag.sameBanks.sentenc.context: Layer 2 Inspector (ZX Spectrum Next): tooltip of the '$12 = $13' chip (two NextRegs holding the same value).

@gfxCommon.layer2.diag.readsPastLayer.ch.context: Layer 2 Inspector (ZX Spectrum Next): short warning chip. The scroll offset makes the display show memory beyond the layer's own banks.

gfxCommon.layer2.diag.readsPastLayer.wid: The X scroll makes the display read source columns 320-511, which come from the three banks after the layer's five (the hardware's X wrap is not a modulo of 320).

@gfxCommon.layer2.diag.readsPastLayer.wi.context: Layer 2 Inspector (ZX Spectrum Next): tooltip of the chip, for the 320- and 640-pixel-wide modes.

gfxCommon.layer2.diag.readsPastLayer.tal: The Y scroll makes the display read source rows 192-254, which come from the bank after the layer's three (the hardware folds rows back by bits 7-6, not modulo 192).

@gfxCommon.layer2.diag.readsPastLayer.ta.context: Layer 2 Inspector (ZX Spectrum Next): tooltip of the chip, for the 256×192 mode.

@gfxCommon.layer2.diag.clipEmpty.chip.context: Layer 2 Inspector (ZX Spectrum Next): short warning chip. The clip window (the rectangle the layer is drawn in) contains no pixel.

gfxCommon.layer2.diag.clipEmpty.sentence: The $18 clip window leaves no pixel of the layer: x1 > x2 or y1 > y2, or it is off the layer.

@gfxCommon.layer2.diag.clipEmpty.sentenc.context: Layer 2 Inspector (ZX Spectrum Next): tooltip of the chip. '$18' is a NextReg; 'x1', 'x2', 'y1', 'y2' are the clip window's coordinates; keep them.

@gfxCommon.layer2.diag.allTransparent.ch.context: Layer 2 Inspector (ZX Spectrum Next): short warning chip. Every pixel of the layer that could show is the transparent colour.

gfxCommon.layer2.diag.allTransparent.sen: Every visible pixel's palette colour equals the global transparency colour $14, so nothing of Layer 2 shows.

@gfxCommon.layer2.diag.allTransparent.se.context: Layer 2 Inspector (ZX Spectrum Next): tooltip of the chip. '$14' is a NextReg and 'Layer 2' a hardware layer name; keep them.

@gfxCommon.layers.priority.blendAdd.context: ZX Spectrum Next layer mixer: name of layer priority mode 110 of NextReg $15, which adds Layer 2's colour to the ULA/tilemap colour. The other modes are letter codes such as 'SLU' and are not translated.

@gfxCommon.layers.priority.blendSub.context: ZX Spectrum Next layer mixer: name of layer priority mode 111 of NextReg $15, which adds the colours and subtracts 5 from each component.

@gfxCommon.layers.blendSource.none.context: ZX Spectrum Next layer mixer: the blend source chosen by NextReg $68 bits 6-5 - here no layer is blended with Layer 2. The other choices are layer names (ULA, tilemap) and stay English. Lower case.

@gfxCommon.layers.blendAdd.context: ZX Spectrum Next: the layer-priority readout in the Layers strip, the Layers document and the pixel probe, for blend mode 110 of NextReg $15. 'Layer 2' is a hardware layer name; keep it.

placeholders.source: What Layer 2 is blended with: 'ULA', 'tilemap', 'ULA + tilemap' or 'none'

@gfxCommon.layers.blendSub.context: ZX Spectrum Next: the layer-priority readout, for blend mode 111 of NextReg $15 (add the colours, subtract 5). 'Layer 2' is a hardware layer name; keep it.

placeholders.source: What Layer 2 is blended with: 'ULA', 'tilemap', 'ULA + tilemap' or 'none'

gfxCommon.layers.why.fallback: fallback $4A: no layer is opaque here

@gfxCommon.layers.why.fallback.context: ZX Spectrum Next pixel probe tooltip on the emulator screen: why this pixel has its colour. No layer has a colour here, so the fallback colour from NextReg $4A shows (keep '$4A'). Starts lower case.

gfxCommon.layers.why.ula: ULA: the top opaque layer in this order

@gfxCommon.layers.why.ula.context: ZX Spectrum Next pixel probe tooltip: the ULA layer (keep the name) supplies this pixel because it is the topmost layer with a colour in the current priority order.

gfxCommon.layers.why.tilemap: tilemap: the top opaque layer in this order

@gfxCommon.layers.why.tilemap.context: ZX Spectrum Next pixel probe tooltip: the tilemap layer (keep the name) supplies this pixel because it is the topmost layer with a colour in the current priority order.

gfxCommon.layers.why.layer2: Layer 2: the top opaque layer in this order

@gfxCommon.layers.why.layer2.context: ZX Spectrum Next pixel probe tooltip: Layer 2 (keep the name) supplies this pixel because it is the topmost layer with a colour in the current priority order.

gfxCommon.layers.why.layer2Priority: Layer 2 priority bit: Layer 2 over every other layer

@gfxCommon.layers.why.layer2Priority.context: ZX Spectrum Next pixel probe tooltip: Layer 2 (keep the name) wins because its palette entry has the priority bit set, which puts it above all other layers.

gfxCommon.layers.why.sprites: sprites: the top opaque layer in this order

@gfxCommon.layers.why.sprites.context: ZX Spectrum Next pixel probe tooltip: the sprite layer (keep 'sprites' as the layer's name) supplies this pixel because it is the topmost layer with a colour in the current priority order.

gfxCommon.layers.why.border: sprite over the border: a sprite shows over the ULA border where the tilemap is transparent

@gfxCommon.layers.why.border.context: ZX Spectrum Next pixel probe tooltip: why a sprite pixel shows in the screen border. 'ULA' and 'tilemap' are layer names; keep them.

@gfxCommon.layers.why.stencil.context: ZX Spectrum Next pixel probe tooltip: stencil mode is on, so the pixel is the bitwise AND of the ULA and tilemap colours. Keep 'ULA', 'tilemap', 'AND' and '$68 bit 0'.

gfxCommon.layers.why.blendAdd: blend: Layer 2 + the blend source, saturated ($15 110)

@gfxCommon.layers.why.blendAdd.context: ZX Spectrum Next pixel probe tooltip: the pixel is Layer 2's colour added to the blend source's, capped at the maximum. '$15 110' is the NextReg and mode; keep it.

@gfxCommon.layers.why.blendSub.context: ZX Spectrum Next pixel probe tooltip: the pixel is Layer 2's colour added to the blend source's, minus 5. '$15 111' is the NextReg and mode; keep it.

@gfxCommon.layers.pill.solo.context: ZX Spectrum Next: pill on the emulator screen telling that the layer debug view changes the picture - one layer is shown alone. Layer names (ULA, tilemap, Layer 2, sprites) stay English.

placeholders.layer: The layer shown alone, e.g. Layer 2

@gfxCommon.layers.pill.soloTransparency.context: ZX Spectrum Next: pill on the emulator screen - one layer is shown alone, and pixels where no layer has a colour are marked.

placeholders.layer: The layer shown alone, e.g. Layer 2

@gfxCommon.layers.pill.hidden.context: ZX Spectrum Next: pill on the emulator screen - some layers are hidden by the debug view.

placeholders.layers: The hidden layers, comma-separated, e.g. ULA, tilemap

@gfxCommon.layers.pill.hiddenTransparenc.context: ZX Spectrum Next: pill on the emulator screen - some layers are hidden, and pixels where no layer has a colour are marked.

placeholders.layers: The hidden layers, comma-separated, e.g. ULA, tilemap

@gfxCommon.layers.pill.transparency.context: ZX Spectrum Next: pill on the emulator screen - pixels where no layer has a colour are marked.

@gfxCommon.layers.view.solo.context: Output line of the 'layers' IDE command, one per layer: this layer is shown alone. The layer name stays English.

placeholders.layer: The layer's name: ULA, Tilemap, Layer 2 or Sprites

@gfxCommon.layers.view.eclipsed.context: Output line of the 'layers' IDE command: this layer is not on screen because another one is shown alone.

placeholders.layer: The layer's name: ULA, Tilemap, Layer 2 or Sprites

@gfxCommon.layers.view.hidden.context: Output line of the 'layers' IDE command: this layer is hidden by the debug view.

placeholders.layer: The layer's name: ULA, Tilemap, Layer 2 or Sprites

@gfxCommon.layers.view.shown.context: Output line of the 'layers' IDE command: this layer is shown.

placeholders.layer: The layer's name: ULA, Tilemap, Layer 2 or Sprites

@gfxCommon.layers.view.transparencyShown.context: Output line of the 'layers' IDE command: pixels where no layer has a colour are painted magenta.

@gfxCommon.layers.view.transparencyNotMa.context: Output line of the 'layers' IDE command: pixels where no layer has a colour are not marked.

gfxCommon.layers.command.unknownLayer: Unknown layer ''{target}'': use ula, tm, l2, spr, all or transparency

@gfxCommon.layers.command.unknownLayer.context: Error of the 'layers' IDE command. The quotes around the typed name are part of the text (written as '' in the message). The listed words are command arguments; keep them.

gfxCommon.layers.command.unknownAction: Unknown action ''{action}'': use on, off or solo

@gfxCommon.layers.command.unknownAction.context: Error of the 'layers' IDE command. The quotes are part of the text (written as '' in the message). 'on', 'off' and 'solo' are command arguments; keep them.
